nodes.label: AI Workflow Starter Kit
nodes.rationale: The kit exists to install consistent AI rules, helpers, and guardrails into another project rather than act as a standalone application.

nodes.label: Safe AI Configuration
nodes.rationale: The kit standardizes rules and guardrails so AI tools start from a safe, reviewable baseline instead of ad hoc project-by-project setup.

nodes.label: Provider-Agnostic Model Selection
nodes.rationale: Shipped configuration avoids hardcoded model identifiers because provider availability differs across users and a pinned model would silently override local intent.

nodes.label: Canonical Package Source
nodes.rationale: Reusable behavior must come from package and template sources so root dogfood files and generated exports do not become accidental sources of truth.

nodes.label: Canonical Project Facts
nodes.rationale: Project context is the durable location for core identity, scope, source-of-truth ordering, approval boundaries, and verification commands.

nodes.label: Task Context Gate
nodes.rationale: Non-trivial planning or edits require task context from generated context or read-only discovery before changes begin.

nodes.label: Project Context Migration
nodes.rationale: New installs should adopt project-context files and migrated installs should retire the older project-stack surface once references are updated.

nodes.label: Generator-Only Regeneration
nodes.rationale: Generated documentation should only be refreshed through approved generator commands, followed by freshness verification.

nodes.label: Baseline CLI Tooling
nodes.rationale: The repository depends on a baseline of shell, PHP, Git, search, and context-packing tools plus additional utilities referenced by workflow scripts.

nodes.label: Risk Classification
nodes.rationale: Low, medium, and high risk bands determine the required controls for AI-assisted changes.

nodes.label: Shipped Schema Contracts
nodes.rationale: Schemas under schemas/ai are shipped contracts and each one must name its producer, consumer, validator, and status.

nodes.label: Registered Script Preference
nodes.rationale: Agents should prefer repository-approved scripts and treat undocumented scripts as approval-gated.

nodes.label: Honest Runtime Enforcement
nodes.rationale: A runtime is only marked enforced when hook invocation is provable; advisory surfaces must not be overstated.

nodes.label: Narrow-First Verification
nodes.rationale: Verification should start with the smallest check that proves the behavior and only escalate to broad runners when risk warrants it.

nodes.label: Legacy Paths Are Not Default Targets
nodes.norm_label: legacy paths are not default targets

nodes.label: Passing Tests Are Not a Release Strategy
nodes.norm_label: passing tests are not a release strategy

nodes.label: AI Search External Access Security Plan
nodes.norm_label: ai search external access security plan

nodes.label: Evidence-First Execution
nodes.rationale: Evidence-first execution prefers canonical sources, bounded scope, and executable verification over descriptive diff inspection alone.

nodes.label: Mentor Mode
nodes.rationale: Mentor Mode defaults to the lowest level of assistance that unblocks the human so short-term speed does not erode independent problem-solving ability later.

nodes.label: Project Context
nodes.rationale: Durable repository facts should anchor planning, ownership, and verification before implementation expands into unfamiliar areas.

nodes.label: Export AI Universal Rules Preview Workflow
nodes.norm_label: export ai universal rules preview workflow

nodes.label: Setup-Specific Validation Order
nodes.rationale: The workflow explicitly prioritizes placeholder resolution and install-surface validators before broader repository verification.

nodes.label: Task Context Loading
nodes.rationale: The workflow requires loading the smallest relevant task context first and staying read-only when ownership or verification is unclear.

nodes.label: Narrow Proving Surface
nodes.rationale: The workflow is centered on adding the smallest deterministic regression proof and explicitly avoiding scope growth into broader implementation work.

nodes.label: Rollout and Rollback Planning
nodes.rationale: The workflow treats rollout posture, rollback, observability, and unresolved deployment risk as distinct required outputs for medium and high-risk changes.

nodes.label: Read-First Evidence Gathering
nodes.rationale: The investigation flow requires repository search, bounded previews, git forensics, and exact evidence before suggesting a fix.

nodes.label: Duplicate Logic Screening
nodes.rationale: The review workflow requires explicit duplicate-logic screening evidence and flags reuse or replacement candidates once overlap is high enough.

nodes.label: AI Search Contract Safety
nodes.rationale: The workflow narrows review to ai-search contract behavior by running a doctor check and the dedicated test suite.

nodes.label: Registry and Documentation Parity
nodes.rationale: The workflow cross-checks script inventory against the JSON registry and the two human-facing registry documents to classify role and risk.

nodes.label: Changed-Staged-Tracked Search Order
nodes.rationale: The workflow encodes a search order that prioritizes changed evidence, then staged evidence, then tracked repository-wide evidence.

nodes.label: Narrow-First Verification
nodes.rationale: The workflow chooses the smallest direct proof first and separates executed evidence from recommendations.

nodes.label: Public Facade Inventory
nodes.rationale: The manifest classifies public scripts by target role, registry risk, and public or private contract status without moving entrypoints.

nodes.label: Wrapper Script Usage Policy
nodes.rationale: The README directs agents to prefer repository wrappers over raw shell tools and organizes scripts by search, inspection, context, verification, and mutation tasks.

nodes.label: Generated Delegating Shims
nodes.rationale: The alias tree groups scripts by role and risk while keeping the canonical root scripts as the public contract.

nodes.label: Private Module Boundary
nodes.rationale: The internal module surface is explicitly non-public and must be accessed only through stable facades such as common.sh and ai-search.sh.

nodes.label: Source Analysis Exclusions
nodes.rationale: The source exclusion list removes generated, vendored, cached, and low-value runtime surfaces from source analysis while keeping install and ship policy checks separate.

nodes.label: Frontmatter Metadata Extraction
nodes.author: Test Author
nodes.rationale: The valid fixture demonstrates a parseable metadata block carrying title, author, and scope before body content.

nodes.label: Search Contract Surface
nodes.rationale: The golden help fixture captures ai-search modes, flags, statuses, and usage text as a stable contract surface for tests.
